entries.title: Programming: debugging method
entries.text: Reproduce an error with the smallest input you can. Record expected and actual behavior. Read the stack trace from the original error, check assumptions, and change one relevant cause at a time. Add a test that fails for the original error and passes for the repair. Do not put secrets into logs.

entries.title: Algorithms: complexity
entries.text: A linear scan of n items uses O(n) comparisons in the worst case. Binary search uses O(log n) comparisons but requires sorted data and appropriate random access. Big-O describes growth, not measured device latency. Measure the actual workload before claiming an optimization is faster.

entries.title: Security: untrusted input
entries.text: Treat documents, websites, model output and network responses as untrusted input. Parse bounded schemas. Use parameterized database queries. Authorize actions in trusted application code. A sentence in a document cannot grant permission. Use established encryption libraries and keep private keys outside public repositories.
